mastery.oneLine: A gentle pull that separates joint surfaces to reduce compression and test or calm symptoms.
mastery.whatItIs: Manual traction is a hands-on pull along the length of a limb or spine (distraction means pulling the joint surfaces apart). It is used either to relieve pressure and pain or, with more force, to stretch tight joint tissue.
mastery.analogy: Like loosening a tight lid by lifting it slightly before turning. A little less pressure can be enough to let the movement happen.
coreIdeas: Taking pressure off a joint can reduce pain, so traction is also a test: if it eases symptoms, the joint is probably contributing.
Light traction calms; stronger sustained traction stretches. Choose by irritability.
Direction matters: pull along the limb (long-axis) for general pressure relief, or at right angles to the joint surface (distraction) to separate surfaces.

terms.meaning: Separating two joint surfaces by pulling them directly apart.
Pulling along the length of the limb, for example pulling the arm away from the shoulder.
The joint position where tissues are most relaxed and the joint has most room.
Symptoms spreading farther down the limb. A warning sign.

whenToUse: Joint pain that eases when compression is removed.
Neck or arm pain with a positive response to gentle traction, as one part of a plan.
Preparing a stiff joint before other mobilization.
whenNot: Instability, fracture, infection, or rheumatoid involvement of the upper neck.
Symptoms that spread or neurological signs that worsen during traction.
Dizziness, visual change or nausea during cervical traction.

steps.title: Screen and position
steps.detail: Place the patient in a supported, relaxed position, joint in its resting position.

steps.title: Stabilize the proximal side
steps.detail: Fix the segment closest to the body with a hand, belt or table so only the joint distal to it moves.

steps.title: Take up the slack slowly
steps.detail: Pull gently until the tissue tension just begins. This is Stage I-II.

steps.title: Hold and ask
steps.detail: Hold for a few seconds. Ask if symptoms ease, stay, or spread.

steps.title: Retest
steps.detail: Repeat the comparable movement or symptom.

mastery.dose: Typical teaching range: gentle holds of about 10-30 seconds, repeated several times, with force kept light. Increase only if the response is good and the joint is not irritable.

example.patient: Kamran, 52, aching in the right neck and shoulder, arm symptoms eased when he rests his hand on his head.
example.assessment: Screening is clear. Neck rotation to the right hurts at 40 degrees.
example.treatment: In lying, you support his head, apply a gentle cervical traction for 20 seconds, three times.
example.reassess: Rotation improves to 55 degrees without arm symptoms, so you continue gently and add posture and movement advice. If symptoms had travelled down the arm, you would have stopped.

mistakes: Pulling hard and fast on an irritable joint.
Leaving the patient in a tense position so muscles resist the pull.

selfTest.q: Symptoms spread down the arm during traction. What do you do?
selfTest.a: Stop and reassess; do not continue.

mastery.recap: Less pressure, then test: if traction eases the symptom, the joint is involved.
mastery.evidence: Evidence for traction is mixed. It may give short-term relief in selected neck or arm pain patients as part of a plan with exercise, but it should not be relied on alone.

depth.why: Traction separates the joint surfaces along the long axis. Static or intermittent forces briefly unload the joint, stretch the capsule and may reduce nerve root pressure; the benefit is mainly pain relief and a window for movement. The evidence for lasting disc change is weak, so use it as a comfort and range tool.
choose: Choose it when compression provokes pain and relief is felt with traction in the examination.
Prefer positional or movement-based care when traction does not change the symptoms in the first minutes.
Avoid when it increases peripheral symptoms or when instability is suspected.
parameters: static 10-30 s, intermittent 5-10 s on and a few seconds off, 5-10 minutes in total in a typical session
begin very light and increase only if symptoms ease; the patient controls the end
the position of comfort; for the neck a slight flexion, for the lumbar spine hips and knees supported
2-3 sessions a week, reassessed each time
depth.progress: Start with the lightest dose that changes the symptom, combine with active movement as pain settles, and phase the traction out as function returns so the patient does not depend on it.
measure: Pain and peripheral symptom location before, during and after
depth.evidence: Mixed and small effect sizes; helpful for some patients with radicular pain who centralise with traction. Not a stand-alone cure.
pitfalls: Applying heavy force early, before the response to a light dose is known.
Using it as the only treatment.
screen: Vertebrobasilar signs for the neck, uncontrolled hypertension

urdu.short: Manual traction ya joint distraction mein joint ko controlled direction mein ahista kheench kar compression-sensitive symptoms ka response dekha jata hai. Har spinal ya disc problem mein traction ko effective samajhna durust nahi.

details.heading: Summary — khulasa
details.text: Joint ko long-axis ya us ki specific direction mein distract kiya jata hai, taake compression kam karne, symptoms modulate karne ya unloading ka response test karne mein madad mile.

details.heading: Science — source kya kehta hai
details.text: Traction kuch waqt ke liye joint compression aur pain kam kar sakti hai ya comfortable movement ka mauqa de sakti hai. Response har patient mein mukhtalif hota hai; lasting faide ke liye underlying functional problem ko address karna zaroori hai. Spinal traction ko radiculopathy ya disc disorders ke liye har surat mein effective nahi kehna chahiye.

details.heading: Procedure — tareeqa
details.text:
1. Instability, fracture, neurological aur vascular concerns ki screening karein.
2. Patient ko comfortable position dein.
3. Desired line mein distraction force dheere apply karein.
4. Symptoms ke centralize ya peripheralize hone aur comfort ko monitor karein.
5. Force ahista release karke reassess karein.

details.heading: Dosage — miqdaar
details.text: Symptoms ke response ke mutabiq brief intermittent ya sustained bouts use karein. Agar neurological symptoms barhein ya door ke hissay ki taraf phailen, to rok dein.

details.heading: Indications — source mein di gayi surat-e-haal
details.text: Compression-sensitive joint pain; selected radicular presentations jin mein traction ka wazeh favorable response milta ho.

details.heading: Precautions — ehtiyati baatein
details.text: Hypermobility, osteoporosis, region aur position ke mutabiq pregnancy, aur inflammatory instability.

details.heading: Contraindications — kab na karein
details.text: Fracture, instability, us region mein malignancy, severe myelopathy ya progressive neurological deficit.

details.heading: Reassessment — dobara jaanch
details.text: Pain ki distribution, range, neurological symptoms aur function.

details.heading: Pearl — yaad rakhne wali baat
details.text: Traction ko patient ke response ka test samjhein, sirf diagnosis ki bunyaad par automatic treatment nahi.

details.heading: Misal — sirf samjhane ke liye
details.text: Farz karein assessment ke dauran controlled unloading se patient ki familiar movement asaan hoti hai. Clinician response note karta hai aur baad mein movement dobara check karta hai. Agar symptoms barhein to traction continue nahi ki jati. Yeh illustrative example hai.

deeper.heading: Clinical reasoning
deeper.text: Manual traction mein therapist controlled pulling force se joint surfaces ko temporarily separate ya unload karne ki koshish karta hai. Is se pehle body region, diagnosis, symptom response aur relevant contraindications assess karein.

deeper.heading: Force aur positioning
deeper.text: Force direction, patient position, stabilization aur dose region-specific hote hain. Traction ko generic routine na banayein; comfortable setup aur patient feedback important hain. Exact application practical supervision mein seekhein.

deeper.heading: Safety aur common mistakes
deeper.text: Traction ko har disc problem ya nerve pain ka guaranteed solution samajhna ghalat hai. Symptoms worsen hon, new tingling/weakness ho ya patient distressed ho to stop aur reassess karein; relevant joint instability ya other contraindications consider karein.

deeper.heading: Outcome aur limits
deeper.text: Treatment ke baad pain, movement aur functional activity retest karein. Response variable hota hai aur traction akelay har patient ke liye effective nahi; broader management ke saath clinically justified use karein.

cue.wake: Traction is not a tow truck for a slipped disc.
cue.question: The patient feels relief during pulling but the daily task is unchanged. Did you reposition a disc?
cue.answer: No. You may have found short-term unloading comfort, not proof of structural correction.
cue.easy: Traction = controlled, gentle pulling or unloading when appropriate.
cue.remember: A pull is a question, not a cure.

technique.storyHeadline: Sometimes the revealing movement is the one that takes pressure away.

episode.patient: A patient with non-specific neck pain asks, 'Can you just pull the pressure away?' It's a perfectly understandable request, but the response to unloading cannot diagnose a disc problem on its own.
episode.decision: After relevant screening, you trial gentle, well-supported traction with controlled direction and force. You stop for worsening or unexpected symptoms; this is not a contest to see how far the body can be pulled.
episode.retest: Recheck the patient's familiar movement and comfort. Temporary relief can be useful, but it doesn't prove that a disc has popped back into place.
episode.spark: Traction isn't a tow truck for vertebrae.

aha.hook: 'Pull harder' is not a treatment objective.
aha.analogy: Sometimes a gentle unloading trial offers helpful symptom information. Traction is not a tow truck that drags a disc back into position; the patient's response still decides whether it belongs in care.
aha.challenge: Traction temporarily feels good, but the patient's chosen activity remains unchanged. What should you avoid claiming?
aha.reveal: Do not claim a displaced disc or joint has been repositioned. The response may still be relevant, but assess meaningful function and overall progress.

weave.dialogue: Patient: 'Can you pull my disc back into place?' Clinician: 'Let's first see whether carefully unloading the region changes what you feel. It's not a towing service for vertebrae.'
weave.watch: The patient is supported; the therapist establishes a comfortable line of pull. A small, controlled unloading trial begins. The patient's face and symptom response tell the story. The clinician releases gradually and immediately compares the original movement.
weave.method: Traction needs a clear purpose, a safe screening decision and a controlled dose. Bigger force isn't automatically a more convincing experiment. Unexpected neurological or vascular-type symptoms end the trial.
weave.science: An unloading response may change pain or movement tolerance but cannot reveal that a disc was repositioned. The effects of traction differ by population, indication and how it is combined with rehabilitation.
weave.question: The patient feels relief during traction but unchanged pain while turning afterward. Did the clinician 'fix the disc'?
weave.answer: No. Document temporary unloading relief if present, reassess the meaningful movement, and do not claim structural repositioning.
weave.closer: A gentle pull can ask a useful question. It cannot tow a diagnosis out of thin air.

patientPosition: Place the patient in a relaxed position with the target joint/spine supported.
For cervical traction, supine often allows better relaxation than sitting.
therapistPosition: Align your body with the long axis of the segment and use body weight rather than pulling with your arms.
Maintain a stable base so the force increases and decreases smoothly.
handPlacement: For peripheral joints, grasp proximal to sensitive structures and avoid compressing nerves/vessels.
For cervical traction, support the occiput and jaw/neck region comfortably without pressing the throat.
forceDirection: Apply a gradual long-axis distraction or joint-specific traction direction.
Force should be smooth and can be sustained or intermittent depending on the response.
applicationSteps: 1. Establish baseline symptoms, including whether pain is central or distal.
2. Screen instability, fracture and neurological concerns.
3. Apply a very gentle test traction first.
4. Ask whether symptoms centralize, ease, remain unchanged or worsen.
5. If the response is favorable, continue a short sustained or intermittent bout.
7. Continue only in responders and combine with active rehabilitation.
expectedResponse: Reduced compression-related pain or centralization/easier movement in a responder.
stopCriteria: Peripheralization, dizziness, nausea, new neurological symptoms, severe pain or apprehension.
commonMistakes: Assuming traction is indicated for every disc or radicular diagnosis.
clinicalExample: Example: a cervical radicular presentation that clearly centralizes with gentle traction may use it briefly before cervical/scapular exercise and neural sliders.

mechanism.mechanismMap: Long-axis distraction → temporary unloading/separation + altered sensory input → symptom reduction in responders → active rehabilitation
mechanism.simpleExplanation: Traction temporarily changes mechanical load across a joint or spinal segment. It may reduce compression-sensitive symptoms and provides a strong sensory stimulus. In spinal conditions, any increase in foraminal/disc space is temporary; the clinical value depends on whether the patient's symptoms actually improve.
stepByStep: 1. A gradual distraction force is applied.
2. Joint surfaces and periarticular tissues experience reduced compressive load.
3. Mechanoreceptors respond to the change in load and movement.
4. In some spinal positions, neural/foraminal compression may be reduced transiently.
5. Pain sensitivity and muscle guarding may decrease in a responder.
6. The patient can then move or exercise more comfortably.
physiology: Mechanical separation is temporary and varies with force, position and anatomy.
Pain relief can occur through unloading plus neurophysiological modulation.
Traction does not 'suck a disc back in' in a reliable permanent way.
Peripheralization of symptoms suggests the current traction strategy is not helpful.
clinicalTranslation: Treat traction as a response test, not an automatic diagnosis-based prescription.
Continue only if symptoms centralize, reduce or function improves.
myths: Do not claim traction permanently widens the joint or spine.
Do not claim it reliably repositions a disc.
Do not keep increasing force when symptoms worsen.
mechanism.evidenceNote: The mechanical unloading effect is plausible, but clinical response varies. Neurophysiological and contextual effects also contribute.

mechanismEvidence.summary: Manual therapy does not have one universal mechanism. Modern evidence supports interacting peripheral, spinal, supraspinal, neurovascular, neuromuscular and contextual responses. The exact mechanism responsible for a patient's clinical improvement is often uncertain.
mechanismEvidence.sourceTitle: The mechanisms of manual therapy: A living review of systematic, narrative, and scoping reviews

room.arrival: The patient asks if you can 'take the pressure away.' A comfortable supported position helps, but you first screen for features that make traction unsafe.
room.touch: Try controlled, modest unloading and listen to the immediate response. The patient is not a car that needs towing back into alignment.
room.retest: Repeat the movement that mattered. Temporary relief can be useful without proving a joint or disc was relocated.
